title: Paloma and the Vector
premise: Casper Dravenmoor, a xenolinguist whose dreams have gone silent in every human tongue, ferries cargo along routes between worlds that have stopped answering. When the name Paloma Vey appears on the manifest of a ship that never flew, he discovers she is a memory-archivist condemned by an interstellar tribunal for preserving testimony of a massacre the Concordance erased. Pursued by enforcer-signals that rewrite the past as they travel, Casper must carry Paloma's archived memories to the relay at the edge of dead space before the signal that would broadcast them decays forever. He reaches the relay and transmits her testimony at the cost of his own last human-language dreams, choosing justice over the self he was.
about_author: Rafael Amberdale is the pen name of a former shipping-log analyst who spent a decade reading manifests from routes no one else remembered flying. They write science fiction about people who keep records the universe would rather lose.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Casper Dravenmoor, running the long route between silent worlds, finds the name Paloma Vey on the manifest of the Meridian Lark—a vessel destroyed before it ever launched. Following the anomaly to a derelict station, he recovers a sealed archive humming with her voice. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: unease curdling into compulsion; a man who has lost his dreams feels something finally calling him back.

chapters.title: Testimony in Dead Tongues
chapters.summary: Decoding the archive, Casper experiences Paloma's recorded memories: she was a tribunal archivist who preserved evidence of the Kestrel Reach massacre the Concordance expunged, and was sentenced to erasure. Enforcer-signals begin rewriting local records to erase Casper too. POV: alternating Casper and Paloma's recordings. Emotional beat: falling in love with a voice from the dead, and terror as duty closes in.

chapters.title: Race Against the Signal
chapters.summary: Casper burns toward the edge-of-dead-space relay as the decay window narrows, while enforcer-ships close in, offering amnesty if he surrenders the archive. A boarding skirmish cripples his ship; he jettisons his own life's logs as decoy data, letting the enemy chase a fabricated Casper. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: sacrifice sharpening into resolve—he stops mourning what he loses and starts spending it.

chapters.title: What the Relay Remembers
chapters.summary: At the failing relay, Casper splices Paloma's testimony into the broadcast lattice as enforcers breach the hull. The transmission goes out across dead space—every silent world hears Kestrel Reach again. The cost: his last human-language dreams burn away in the uplink. Epilogue: tribunals reopen; Casper, dreaming now only in Paloma's tongue, flies on carrying her name. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into purpose; love outlasting erasure.
